title: Blender 5.1.2 P0 extensions — tested Python calls and context boundaries
content:
Verified 2026-11-15 on macOS Blender 5.1.2 / Python 3.13.9: Texel Density Checker 2026.1.1 and 3D Print Toolbox 1.5.0 registered and ran as bl_ext.user_default.texel_density_checker and bl_ext.user_default.print3d_toolbox. Official package hashes and installed source files match; vendor code was not patched. A fresh process confirmed saved enablement.

object.texel_density_check works in background on an active UV mesh. Set scene.td.units='1' for px/m and an explicit texture size. A 1 m square with full UVs and a 1024 texture measured 1024 px/m; object scale 2 measured 512. The native object.texel_density_set fails without context.area. Through MCP, use a real existing window/VIEW_3D/WINDOW region with temp_override; the tested setter changed 1024 to 512 px/m and UV width to 0.5. This is not headless setter support.

mesh.print3d_check_all/check_solid/check_degenerate analyze the active object. scene.print3d_toolbox.get_report() returns structured rows. A closed 1 m cube reported 0 non-manifold edges, volume 1 m3, area 6 m2; an open cube reported 4 boundary edges; a collinear triangle reported 1 zero-area face. Volume/area operators aggregate selection, unlike analysis checks.

Temporary-fixture UI tests restored original geometry, selection, editor types and dirty flag. An independent one-scene/one-mesh GLB passed Khronos validation and Three.js loading. These supplement existing GLB QA; other extension features, full-library appearance/performance and devices were not validated.

metadata.scope: Version-specific reusable operator and context evidence, not universal compatibility or live installation state on other machines
metadata.evidence: Official package provenance, bounded source inspection, numeric positive/negative fixtures, native UI MCP calls, fresh-process readback and independent GLB validation
